subject: Post-call: edge-case SLO probes and hosted switch feasibility
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: edge-case SLO probes and hosted switch feasibility

Hi Sanjay / team,

Thanks again for carving out time this morning — great alignment on the business case and a clear set of technical concerns to validate before a hosted switch. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks:

Summary of asks from Acme:
- End-to-end p95 and p99 latency targets for the user-facing pipeline (in-region): p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 420ms
- Sustained throughput target: 1,200 QPS for inference calls during peak windows
- Concurrent streaming sessions: up to 250 concurrent streaming connections with average chunk size of ~1.2KB
- Failover behavior expectations and cold-start tolerances for short bursts

What we (Redwood) will deliver:
1) A short PoC (3 weeks) to validate E2E p95/p99 across your real traffic profile — recommended: staged test traffic + one week of shadow traffic in production.
2) A small telemetry package showing tail latencies, variance by region/route, and KV cache hit-rate.
3) A runbook mapping batching/concurrency knobs and the expected unit-cost tradeoffs.

Immediate asks from us to you:
- Sample traffic/trace file (minute-level) for a typical workday peak and a 1-hour spike (we discussed the anonymized trace export). Preferred formats: CSV with timestamp, request_size_bytes, response_tokens, model, route OR JSONL with same fields.
- Current provider latency export (p95/p99 by minute or 5-minute window) for the last 7 days.
- Any strict SLA blackout windows or regional routing constraints.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short PoC proposal PDF and a one-sheet showing how we measure p95/p99.

Proposed next meeting: Wed 2027-04-28 10:00am PT for a 30-min runbook + infra owners sync. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-ai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: 2027-04-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: edge-case SLO probes and hosted switch feasibility

Jordan — thanks for the recap. That captures it. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The p95/p99 targets are strict for the US-east region only for now; we can be more relaxed for EU/APAC during the PoC.
- For throughput, the 1,200 QPS is burstable for ~10 minutes; our baseline sustained is closer to 350 QPS.
- Streaming sessions: our product uses server-sent events with small deltas (we send ~3–5 chunks per second per session).

I’m attaching the latency export from our current provider (acme-current-latency-sample.csv) and a small traffic profile (acme-traffic-profile.json). Files are sanitized.

We’re happy to do shadow testing. One ask: can Redwood measure both tail latencies and per-request cost so we can weigh the economics against the SLA?

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, Acme AI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: edge-case SLO probes and hosted switch feasibility

Perfect — got the attachments, thanks. Quick answers:

- Yes, our standard PoC telemetry includes p50/p90/p95/p99, plus per-request CPU/GPU time and per-token cost estimate. We’ll provide a short cost delta summary (hosted vs your current provider) with the PoC closeout.
- For the US-east-only gating, we’ll pin the test traffic to that region and keep EU/APAC muted.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Today: ingest the files you shared and run a simulation to estimate batching impacts (we’ll share a preliminary model by EOD tomorrow).
2) Tue-Wed next week: run a 48-hour shadowing window at 10x compressed sample traffic to stress tail behaviour.
3) Week after: live 1-week shadow in production with telemetry and rollback guardrails.

Marissa — can you draft the PoC SOW and procurement checklist (3–4 items) so we can get procurement looped in quickly? Ben — FYI on potential commercial levers here (reserved vs committed throughput). Karthik — I’ll need a short note from you on streaming concurrency limits and how we’ll configure chunk buffering for SSE.

Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: edge-case SLO probes and hosted switch feasibility

Quick technical note on streaming concurrency and chunking:
- For SSE-style streams sending 3–5 chunks/sec per session, we recommend configuring our streaming pool with an initial concurrency cap of 300 streams and a per-stream buffer budget of ~8KB before backpressure. That keeps tail amplification low.
- If Acme can send a small sample of raw chunk sizes (distribution), we can model the KV caching and expected per-token latency delta.
- We’ll instrument continuous batching with a 5–15ms window for short requests; long requests (>2s) will be routed to a low-latency pathway to avoid head-of-line blocking.

I’ll prep a short config snippet for the PoC SOW.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
